citation: Silva et al., Experimental Validation of a Spoke Type Ferrite Permanent Magnet Machine Design for Heavy-Duty Traction Applications

reported_findings.fault_design_method: Optimize torque after symmetric short-circuit event; demagnetization safety factor is minimum temperature-dependent Hcj divided by bulk PM field magnitude.

limitations: Prototype physically tested across normal operating points; short-circuit demagnetization and post-fault torque were evaluated in FEM/design workflow, not by an executed physical fault campaign described in the paper.
The 1.3 demagnetization and 2.0 mechanical safety factors are study-specific design constraints, not universal limits.
A few efficiency operating points are not a matched whole-mission-cycle result.
External evidence, not Luminous physical evidence.

citation: Liu et al., A review of structural design for reduced-rare-earth permanent magnet motors in new energy vehicles
reported_findings: Compares SynRM, SRM, EESM, induction and ferrite-assisted architectures.
Identifies irreversible demagnetization of low-coercivity magnets and mechanical deformation of flux-barrier rotors as persistent challenges.
Discusses optimized flux barriers, spoke topology, direct oil cooling, temperature-aware control, grain-boundary diffusion and iron nitride magnets.
limitations: Review-level synthesis; qualitative topology ranking is not a matched experimental result.

citation: Li et al., Enhancing coercivity and thermal stability in high-remanence Nd-Fe-B magnets via TbF3 grain boundary diffusion
limitations: Tb is a heavy rare earth; this route is not rare-earth-free or automatically lower-critical-element.
Material-level coercivity/thermal stability does not establish motor post-fault service.
Study-specific material and diffusion process; not Luminous evidence.

citation: Park et al., Rare-Earth-Free Iron-Based Permanent Magnets: Progress, Challenges, and Perspectives
reported_findings: Reviews Fe-Co, ordered Fe-Ni/tetrataenite, alpha-double-prime Fe16N2, iron phosphides and borides.
Experimental translation remains constrained by phase stability, grain size and processing.
Fe16N2 phase control and elevated-temperature stability remain key commercialization barriers.
limitations: Theoretical or thin-film magnetic values are not equivalent to stable bulk traction magnet components.

citation: Zhao et al., Optimizing alpha-double-prime Fe16N2 as a permanent magnet via alloying
limitations: Computational screening, not bulk magnet or motor experiment; stability and manufacturability are not established.
